messages:
emily-cs: FYI customer Acme reports duplicate partial outputs + double billing after an SSE disconnect/reconnect. They say client reconnects with a resume token and then sees overlapping chunks.
maria-eng: Can you paste the minimal repro and SDK version? Also whether they're using exponential backoff or instant retry.
acme-dev: Using our in-house SSE client v0.9.1. Heartbeat every 30s. When we see a 502 we immediately reopen the connection and send resume_token + last_seq=42. Server replies 200 resume_ack then we get chunks starting at seq=40..44 again (40-41 are duplicates). We see duplicate tokens billed.
nate-eng: Do you have the exact HTTP responses? Are we returning a resume window or a full stream from an earlier offset? :eyes:
acme-dev: Snippet below — we include resume headers on reconnect:
```
GET /v1/stream?resume=true HTTP/1.1
Authorization: Bearer sk-****
X-Resume-Token: rtk_abc123
X-Last-Seq: 42
```
Server initial response: 200 OK, then SSE events starting with `event: chunk` seq:40
jun-sre: Two quick hypotheses: (1) client reconnects before server had persisted last_seq so server replayed earlier items; (2) our resume logic accepts token but misaligns seq base (off-by-N). Also check client-side buffering of un-acked chunks.
maria-eng: Can you share the stream logs showing seq headers + any resume token id? Need server-side trace for the request id that handled the reconnect.
acme-dev: I attached a sanitized log to the ticket (link: https://acme.example/logs/stream-2345). It shows server reconnect handling id=svc-99 and the server emits chunk seq 40..44 after resume.
emily-cs: Ticket created: CS-4321. Ops bot assigned to eng-runtime. ops-bot: Created incident CS-4321 and pinged #eng-runtime :thumbsup:
nate-eng: Immediate mitigation: instruct client to ignore any incoming chunk whose seq <= last_acked_seq. Also add a short randomized backoff (100-500ms) before reconnect to reduce races where server still finalizing the previous session.
maria-eng: We'll look at server logs for svc-99. If resume token mapping was updated but seq base not advanced, that's a clear off-by-one. Also check whether KV-caching of prefix was flushed on the previous close.
jun-sre: For billing: we'll need to correlate token+seq ranges to charge windows. If duplicates are caused by server replay, we'll refund duplicates for that session and then push a fix.
acme-dev: Appreciate that. We can add client-side dedupe but would prefer server guarantees for resume semantics.
emily-cs: Action items summarized:
- acme-dev: share full SSE client logs + exact timestamps (done).
- eng-runtime (maria-eng, nate-eng): triage svc-99 logs, confirm whether seq base was moved and whether resume handler returned an earlier cursor.
- jun-sre: prepare prospective refund for duplicated seq ids and escalate billing if needed.
- emily-cs: will update customer by EOD with preliminary findings.
maria-eng: If you can reproduce locally, please include a minimal cURL/websocket equivalent. Example repro we use:
```
# simulate reconnect with resume header
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-..." -H "X-Resume-Token: rtk_abc123" -H "X-Last-Seq: 42" https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream?resume=true
```
nate-eng: Also check server deploy history for the timeframe — a recent change to KV flush semantics could explain it.
acme-dev: Will try client-side dedupe as a temporary workaround and report back.
emily-cs: Thanks everyone — I'll post updates in this thread. Next update by 2345679310 or sooner. :raised_hands:
